KCNQ1, which is known to encode an ion channel involved in the regulation of insulin secretion, is strongly associated with susceptibility to diabetes in Japanese, Danish and Singaporean populations, and that the association is replicated in several independent studies.
the KCNQ1 gene, a strong candidate for type 2 diabetes susceptibility, was identified through a large-scale genome-wide association study (GWAS) in Japanese individuals.
we have identified a strong association of SNPs in the KCNQ1 gene with type 2 (noninsulin-dependent) diabetes in Japanese, Singaporean, and Danish populations.

the association between KCNQ1 polymorphism and susceptibility to type 1 diabetes.

the association of SNPs in KCNQT1 with type 2 diabetic susceptibility in East Asians and Europeans.

KCNQ1 is strongly associated with type-2 diabetes, and this association is replicated across multiple populations, and that this association is independent of the association with type-2-diabetes in the neighboring region of chromosome 11p15.5.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
KCNQ1 is a strong susceptibility gene for type 2 diabetes.
KCNQ1 is associated with type 1 and type 2 diabetes, but the association with type 2 is more consistent and stronger than with type 1 diabetes.
KCNQ1 SNPs are associated with type 1 diabetes and type 2 diabetes, and that the same KCNQ1 SNP (rs2237895) may contribute to both type 1 diabetes risk and type 2 disease risk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the KCNQ1 gene is a major susceptibility gene for type 2 diabetes across multiple populations.
the association between SNPs in KCNQT1 and type 2 diabetes is consistent in East Asian, European, and South Asian populations.
the KCNQ1 gene, which encodes an inward rectifying potassium ion channel, may play an important role in susceptibility to type 1 diabetes.
